title: Wait for a quorum of replica acknowledgements

blocks.text: The order store keeps every record on several replicas. A write is confirmed to the caller once a quorum of replicas has acknowledged it; the rest catch up later. Replicas acknowledge from their own threads, and a fast one may acknowledge before the writer has even started to wait.

Two reports came in after a replica failure last week. Writes that had exactly the quorum of replicas behind them were reported as failed. And just after a slow replica went down, one write was confirmed although only one replica had stored it.

Finish `acksForNextWrite()` and `awaitQuorum(...)` in `src/main/java/practice/QuorumWriter.java`. `write(...)` already sends the record and passes each replica an acknowledgement that releases one permit. When you're done, a write is confirmed exactly when a quorum of replicas acknowledged that write, and a write that can't reach a quorum returns `false` once `timeoutMillis` has passed. About two lines in total.

cases.says: writes succeed one after another when every replica acknowledges, whether before or after the writer waits
a write succeeds with exactly a quorum of acknowledgements and no more
an acknowledgement that arrives after its write completed does not count towards the next write
a write that cannot reach a quorum returns false once its timeout has passed

origin.section: A Semaphore Keeps a Release Nobody Waited For, Which Makes It a Signal

concepts: A semaphore that starts at -k needs k+1 releases before a single acquire succeeds.
A release with nobody waiting is kept as a permit, so a semaphore can count signals from other threads, and leftover permits carry over to the next use.
